Cc: Elliot Grant <elliot@foundrystartup.io>
Date: Sun, 24 Aug 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Combining Foundry voucher with Redwood sandbox credits?

Hi Priyom,

Hope you’re well — Foundry Spark is kicking off a new cohort and several of our startups want to evaluate Redwood for production inference. We typically issue a $7k program voucher per company as part of onboarding. A few of the founders also qualify for your public sandbox credits (the $500 developer credits). Before we schedule demos, we wanted to clarify whether Foundry vouchers and Redwood sandbox credits can stack for a single account, or if your system treats them as mutually exclusive promotions.

A few specifics:
- Some startups want the voucher applied to a single account and keep the sandbox credit active for a parallel test project.
- One sponsor wants to be invoiced for overage beyond the voucher; does Redwood support sponsor billing/POs in that model?

Attached: foundry_program_summary.pdf (brief program overview).

Thanks — if stacking is possible we’ll expedite allotting the vouchers so onboarding can start next week.

Best,
Sana Rao
Partnerships, Foundry Spark Accelerator

Attachment: foundry_program_summary.pdf
From: priyom_das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
To: Sana Rao <sana@foundryspark.co>
Cc: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 24 Aug 2025 12:35:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Combining Foundry voucher with Redwood sandbox credits?

Hi Sana — great to hear from you, excited about the cohort. Short answer: our standard policy is that promotional vouchers and public sandbox credits do not stack automatically on the same billing account because it creates ambiguous unit economics and affects quota enforcement. That said, we can make partner exceptions in controlled cases.

Options we can offer immediately:
1) Separate accounts: We can apply the Foundry voucher to the company’s primary account and leave a separate sandbox/test account with the $500 credits. This is simplest operationally but requires the founders to manage two accounts.
2) One-off stack exception: For strategic programs we can allow the Foundry voucher to stack with the sandbox credit up to a capped combination amount (we typically cap at $5k of Redwoods-covered consumption beyond the voucher). This requires approvals from Sales + Finance and a short amendment to the standard voucher terms.
3) Sponsor billing: We can accept sponsor invoicing for overages but it requires a PO up front and sponsor setup in our billing system — finance will require a sponsor contract and payment terms.

If Foundry prefers option 2, can you confirm the list of startups and an expected consumption profile (months 1–3)? I’ve looped in Ben (Sales Ops) to estimate the cap and Lauren/Marissa for billing & legal staging once we have names.

Thanks — I can jump on a 20-min call tomorrow if useful.

— Priyom Das
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Email: priyom_das@redwood.com
Phone: (415) 555-0192
From: Sana Rao <sana@foundryspark.co>

Subject: Re: Combining Foundry voucher with Redwood sandbox credits?

Thanks Priyom,

We’d like to pursue option 2 (one-off stack exception) for six startups initially — estimated combined consumption per startup is modest: ~2M tokens/month in month 1, ramping to ~6M tokens/month by month 3. Foundry is comfortable with the $5k cap you mentioned but we’d prefer the cap to be per-company, not pooled, if possible. Sponsor billing will be used for anything above the cap (Foundry will be the sponsor for cohort-wide shared services).

Can you confirm the timeline for approvals and what documentation you’ll need from us (company names, expected start dates, PO template)? Also — do you require companies to be on a particular plan or tier to qualify for stacking?

Appreciate the quick turnaround — if you can confirm by EOD tomorrow we’ll finalize the participant list.

Best,
Sana

Thanks for the context, Priyom. I’m OK approving a per-company stack exception with the following conditions:

1) Cap: $5,000 Redwood-covered stacking per company (not pooled).
2) Timebox: Applies for the first 90 days from account activation.
3) Metrics: We’ll collect token usage by account; if a company exceeds 90 days or significantly exceeds the profile (>2x expected in month 1), we’ll convert them to sponsor-billed or a paid tier.
4) Legal/Amendment: Marissa, please draft a short amendment that references the voucher ID, per-company cap, and timebox. We’ll require an e-signature from the founder or sponsor.
5) Finance: Lauren, we need sponsor PO flow for overages and a billing contact for Foundry. Also confirm whether we can route sponsor invoices to a third-party sponsor on behalf of the startups.

Ben
